Our history and heritage

A long-standing home for rubber research.

Bisianumu has an important place in Papua New Guinea’s rubber story. The Bisianumu Rubber Experiment Station was established during the 1950s on the Sogeri Plateau, at an elevation of approximately 1,800 feet above sea level. The plateau is recognised as an important rubber-producing area.

In the early 1980s, the Bisianumu Rubber Development Section of the Department of Agriculture and Livestock was described as the country’s only experiment station working entirely on rubber research. This history reflects Bisianumu’s role in the development and study of rubber in Papua New Guinea.

Today, the plantation’s trees, harvesting activities and people continue to tell the story of practical work connected to this important crop. The photographs throughout this website offer a glimpse of rubber tapping, collection and transport.

✳Established in the 1950s · Sogeri Plateau, Papua New Guinea

The work behind the harvest

Every stage has a purpose.

Natural rubber is the result of a sequence of practical tasks. Here is a simple look at the work shown across our plantation photographs.

Stage 01

Tapping the trees

A careful cut in the bark allows latex to flow into a collection cup.

Stage 02

Collecting rubber

Collected material is gathered from the tapping area for handling.

Stage 03

Preparing the harvest

Rubber is gathered into suitable containers and sacks for easier handling.

Stage 04

Moving the load

Transport and equipment help move the collected harvest out of the field.
